preparations.context: The window repair leaves packing and cleaning cloths to put away.
The welcome board is painted; its supplies still cover the workbench.
The pastry shelf is ready, but its delivery still needs sorting.
The lamps are lit; their packing and polishing supplies need clearing.
The worktop is steady, and its repair supplies must go back into storage.
The market delivery leaves produce, packing, and a broken pot to clear.
The shelf is secure; clear the broken crock and sort the remaining stock.
The first menu is written, leaving drawing and cleaning supplies to clear.
The new bowls are arranged; unpack the remaining plates and bread supplies.
The table and chairs are restored; clear their cloths and repair supplies.
The recipe corner is ready; sort the loose pages and cabinet-cleaning cloths.
The shared table is open, leaving its covers and welcome supplies to sort.
The courtyard path is clear; move the gathered leaves and cleaning cloths.
The herbs are planted, leaving pot packing and planting supplies to store.
The door hood is repaired; clear the spare shingles and drying cloths.
The outdoor tables are set; clear the leaves and sort the lunch supplies.
The family recipes are pinned up; unpack the supplies for their first trials.
The tasting plates are ready; sort their packing and the tasting supplies.
The drinks cabinet is stocked; clear the broken crock and tied supplies.
The supper menus are printed; clear their packing and table-setting supplies.
The invitations are delivered; sort the spare envelopes and gate towels.
The serving station is ready, but its covers and food supplies still need sorting.
The lights and flowers are in place; clear the stem trimmings and spare cloths.
The bistro is ready for the supper; clear the final flower trimmings and serving supplies.

season.departure: The pickle barrel is empty until next winter.
The forage basket waits for next spring.

mixed_bean-soup-bread-bowl.name: Bean soup in a bread bowl

characters.name: Mara
characters.introduction: I am Mara. I keep the bistro open and make room for neighbours who want a meal or a quiet seat. Help me try a few servings as we prepare the house.

characters.name: Ilie
characters.introduction: I am Ilie, the baker. I bring bread and the notebook where my family kept its dishes. There is room on those pages for what we learn here.

characters.name: Eszter
characters.introduction: I am Eszter. I make the bowls and plates. A useful dish should sit well on the table and leave room for the person beside you.

characters.name: Sorin
characters.introduction: I am Sorin. I help at the bistro between deliveries around the neighbourhood. I know the steep streets, the quiet doors, and where to stop for lunch.

characters.name: Adrian
characters.introduction: I am Adrian. I travel with Monica and Janos. We are checking a few reports from the cathedral beyond the village. We may need provisions for several days at a time.

characters.name: Monica
characters.introduction: I am Monica. I check the paths while Adrian and Janos compare their notes. The old cathedral has more entrances than our map shows. A supply pack lets us stay a few days to look.

characters.name: Janos
characters.introduction: I am Janos. I study the marks in old stonework. Adrian and Monica help me examine the nearby cathedral. Its records leave a few questions, and a long visit needs proper meals.

characters.name: Ionatan
characters.introduction: I am Ionatan, a property agent from another country. I am travelling to the nearby castle to close a real-estate deal with a local noble. I have time for one proper dinner before I leave.

characters.name: Vlad

diet.name: Red wine and meat, no garlic

arrival.speaker: mara
arrival.text: A carriage has stopped at the gate. Count Vlad sends word that he will dine with us tonight.

arrival.speaker: vlad
arrival.text: Baron, officially. Count, in spirit. I read your new chalk menu by lamplight from my carriage. I dislike the sun, so I approve of a bistro that serves supper late.

characters.introduction: Count Vlad, if you please. My castle is outside the village, so I seldom dine here. A meat dish and red wine will suit me. The country roads have given me quite an appetite.

characters.name: Elisabeta

diet.name: Red wine and meat, no garlic

arrival.speaker: eszter
arrival.text: Countess Elisabeta is visiting her land again. She asked whether our front room is quiet.

arrival.speaker: elisabeta
arrival.text: Quiet, clean, and well lit. I shall read my estate papers here with a glass of red wine. Red suits me. It always has.

characters.introduction: I am Countess Elisabeta. I have land nearby, though my visits are infrequent. Please bring a meat dish and red wine. I shall review the estate papers after dinner.

characters.name: Mina
characters.introduction: My name is Mina. My fiancé Ionatan came here to sign a property contract, but his letters stopped. Doctor Avram has come with me to find him. I eat no meat or fish; eggs and dairy are welcome.

characters.name: Avram
characters.introduction: I am Doctor Avram, professional physician and amateur solomonar. I am travelling with Mina to find Ionatan. We will stay together while we ask about the road to the castle.

characters.name: Dochia
characters.introduction: I am Dochia. I keep sheep on the hill above the village, and I wear all my sheepskins until the weather proves that it deserves fewer. I took one off this morning. The weather has not earned another.

characters.name: Victor
characters.introduction: I am Victor. I study anatomy at the college and work late in its old laboratory. Last week one of my projects sat up on the table. It was only a soufflé, but my landlady still screamed.

characters.name: Ana
characters.introduction: I am Ana. I work nights at the clinic, so this is my breakfast. Every Saint Andrew’s Eve I hang garlic on the ward door. The doctor laughs at me, but none of my patients has ever been bitten.

characters.name: Costel
characters.introduction: I am Costel. I mend clocks and build small brass automata in the shop by the well. If you hear ticking under my coat, it is a mechanical sparrow. It likes bright eyes and shiny spoons, so keep an eye on both.

characters.name: Bela
characters.introduction: I am Bela. I keep the old churchyard on the hill. I sleep through the day, so please do not knock before dusk. At night I walk between the graves and wish each one a good night. They are the quietest neighbours in the village, and the best listeners.

characters.name: Sânziana
characters.introduction: I am Sânziana. I sell flowers from the cart by the church. On Midsummer Eve I weave crowns of yellow bedstraw and dance in the meadow until dawn. My sisters dance too. Nobody has ever counted all of us at once.

arrival.speaker: eszter
arrival.text: The front room is ready, and the first flowers have come to see it. This is Sânziana, from the flower cart by the church.

arrival.speaker: sanziana
arrival.text: Eszter promised me a jug for the counter. I promised her flowers that last until midsummer. After that, they make their own plans.

characters.name: Dorian
characters.introduction: I am Dorian. I live in the house with the green door. My fortune leaves me free for fine suppers, good company, and very little work. People say I have not aged since they were children. My portrait in the attic does all the worrying for me.

arrival.speaker: mara
arrival.text: Dorian has asked for a seat under the new lamps. He says that good light is wasted on an empty chair.

arrival.speaker: dorian
arrival.text: I dined in this room when your grandmother ran it, Mara. It has hardly changed. Neither have I.

arrival.speaker: mara
arrival.text: I will pretend that I did not hear that. Sit down, and I will bring the menu.

characters.name: Ileana
characters.introduction: I am Ileana, the seamstress. I finish every spindle before Maundy Thursday, because that night Joimărița checks the houses for idle spinners. She has never visited my house. She has visited my brother twice.

arrival.speaker: ilie
arrival.text: Ileana sews the aprons for half the village. She heard that we have a real kitchen now.

arrival.speaker: ileana
arrival.text: I heard that you have four aprons and eight stains. I brought thread. Finish your work before Thursday, and nobody gets into trouble.

characters.name: Cezar
characters.introduction: I am Cezar, the night watchman. I walk the village from dusk to dawn. Some people say that I do it asleep. That is not true. I am only resting my eyes, and my feet know the way.

arrival.speaker: sorin
arrival.text: This is Cezar. He watches the street at night, and he saw the kitchen lights from the square.

arrival.speaker: cezar
arrival.text: Good evening. Or good morning. I lose track. A warm plate at the end of my round would be very welcome.

arrival.speaker: sorin
arrival.text: He says that at noon too.

characters.name: Cătălina
characters.introduction: I am Cătălina. I ring the church bell, and when hail clouds come over the hill, I ring until they turn back. The old women say that solomonari ride those clouds. I say that they can ride somewhere else.

diet.name: Orthodox fast, fish allowed outside Lent

arrival.speaker: mara
arrival.text: Cătălina rings the bell at the church. She heard that the shared table is open.

arrival.speaker: catalina
arrival.text: I heard it from the bell tower. I hear everything from the bell tower. Save me a seat by the door, in case the hail comes.

characters.name: Bran
characters.introduction: I am Bran. I drive the night bus to the town and back. On my days off, I ride my horse through the woods. I always wear this scarf, because my neck gets cold. Please do not ask more questions about my neck.

arrival.speaker: sorin
arrival.text: This is Bran. He drives the night bus. Once he gave me a lift, and my bicycle too.

arrival.speaker: bran
arrival.text: From tomorrow, the bus stops by the square for a loaf of bread. The horse prefers apples, but the horse does not drive.

characters.name: Mama
characters.introduction: I am Mara’s mother. I keep the kitchen of our flat in the city, and my mother’s recipes in my head.

characters.name: Tata
characters.introduction: I am Mara’s father. I have opinions about carols, roofs, and the price of everything.

chapters.title: Open the shutters
chapters.objective: Make the neglected front room ready to greet neighbours.
chapters.opening: Dust, webs, and a broken pane keep the street outside. Mara wants the front room to welcome people again.
chapters.payoff: The front room is clean, lit, and free of webs, and Ilie has a place for his bread on the counter.

closing.speaker: mara
closing.text: Look at it. Clean glass, a mended board, pastries on the shelf, and both lamps lit.

closing.speaker: ilie
closing.text: I will keep bread on the counter, where people can reach it. That is my first promise to this room.

closing.speaker: sorin
closing.text: The spiders left with the webs. Well, all but the small one under the shelf.

closing.speaker: eszter
closing.text: Let it stay. Every good room has one quiet guest.

chapters.title: A kitchen for everyone
chapters.objective: Arrange a shared kitchen where anyone can help.
chapters.opening: The front room is ready, but the kitchen is not. A shared menu needs a steady worktop, fresh produce, and shelves within reach.
chapters.payoff: The team can cook together, and the first menu explains each dish.

closing.speaker: mara
closing.text: A steady worktop, a produce shelf, jars above, and a menu by the door. We can cook here together now.

closing.speaker: sorin
closing.text: And explain it. On every street, people ask me what zacuscă is. Now they can point at the picture.

closing.speaker: ilie
closing.text: A menu is a promise. Tomorrow we find out if we can keep it.

chapters.title: Around one table
chapters.objective: Make shared seating that is useful and welcoming.
chapters.opening: The food is ready, but the neighbours need a place to sit together. The old long table and the red chairs wait under a dust sheet.
chapters.payoff: Eszter’s tableware sets every place, and the recipe corner keeps room for memories.

closing.speaker: eszter
closing.text: Each place has a bowl and a cup. None of them match, and all of them belong.

closing.speaker: ilie
closing.text: The notebook is on the cabinet. Somebody has already written their aunt’s name beside the papanași.

closing.speaker: mara
closing.text: Then the table is open. Anyone who wants company can find it here.

chapters.title: The courtyard
chapters.objective: Open an outdoor space where everyone can gather and move easily.
chapters.opening: Behind the kitchen, a courtyard sleeps under the leaves. With a clear path and a dry door, the bistro can serve outside.
chapters.payoff: Sorin’s practical help clears the way, and the courtyard is ready for outdoor service.

closing.speaker: sorin
closing.text: I walked the route with a full tray. Gate to door, door to tables, and nothing in the way.

closing.speaker: eszter
closing.text: The herbs are by the door, and the new hood keeps the rain off the step.

closing.speaker: mara
closing.text: Then we can serve outside. Thank you, Sorin. You found every loose stone before a guest did.

chapters.title: Recipes to share
chapters.objective: Test the dishes of the neighbourhood and write them down.
chapters.opening: Neighbours have started to bring their own recipes. Each one needs a tasting, a label, and a place on the menu.
chapters.payoff: The supper menu shows each dish, and neighbours can find their own recipes on it.

closing.speaker: ilie
closing.text: Every recipe on the wall has a name beside it. My grandmother is on there twice.

closing.speaker: eszter
closing.text: And every dish on the menu has a picture and a label, so nobody has to guess.

closing.speaker: sorin
closing.text: A neighbour found her plum dumplings on the menu today. She read it out loud to the whole courtyard.

closing.speaker: mara
closing.text: That is the menu I wanted. Not ours. Everyone’s.

chapters.title: The first community supper
chapters.objective: Bring every preparation together and welcome the guests.
chapters.opening: The rooms are ready and the menu is printed. Now the street needs invitations, a serving station, and the last few flowers.
chapters.payoff: Mara and the team have prepared the bistro for the community supper.

closing.speaker: sorin
closing.text: Every invitation is delivered. Some people asked twice if they really need to bring only an appetite.

closing.speaker: eszter
closing.text: The flowers are short, the lights are on, and every dish on the serving table has its label.

closing.speaker: mara
closing.text: Then we are ready. Let us open the doors.

finale.title: Supper at the bistro

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Look at them. The front room is full, and the courtyard too.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: We opened the shutters and lit the room. Then we made a kitchen where everyone could help.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: We set one long table for everyone, and then we carried it out into the courtyard.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: And the recipes came from every street on my route. Half the menu has a neighbour’s name on it.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Tonight is the supper that we planned together. Tomorrow the bistro stays open, and every neighbour knows the way.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Then I will start the dough early. Somebody will want bread for breakfast.

finale.ending: The supper is served, and the bistro stays open.

work.summary: Replace one broken pane. Prepare and repaint the existing frame and shutters. Keep the sound window structure.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: That window has a cracked pane and a corner missing. The draught reaches all the way to the counter.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: I brought new glass on the bike. Very slowly. The ladder will have to walk.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: And I have cobalt paint for the frame and the shutters. The bistro can greet the street again.

work.summary: Sand and repaint the existing sound welcome board. Add a small flower motif.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: The wooden board is sound. It only needs a new surface.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Folk flowers, red ones, like the old plates. Miez can supervise the painting.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Our black cat has already inspected the empty pastry shelf.

work.summary: Clean the existing pastry shelf. Add a tray, a liner, and the first pastry display.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: This shelf is low enough for everyone to see the pastries.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: And high enough to keep your elbow out of the walnuts.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: A thoughtful design. Pastries need cream, so I will bring a milk churn from the dairy.

work.summary: Mount and connect two supplied lamps. Fit bulbs and check the existing connections.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: The lamps are ready. Shall we put one above each small table?

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Yes, and keep the corner warm and quiet.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: A seat for a quick lunch, and a seat for a long conversation.

work.summary: Stabilize the existing worktop. Repair and seal its damaged edge, then polish the existing pans.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: A steady worktop makes a calm kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: I have sealed the edge. Leave room at the end for a hen’s nest. Fresh eggs keep a kitchen honest.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Now there is space to prepare tomorrow together.

work.summary: Buy one small basket of vegetables and garlic. Prepare the first display and preserves batch.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: The market sent a whole vegetable crate: potatoes, cabbages, and more peppers than my basket could hold.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: We can roast a batch and make a produce shelf.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Good. A jar of zacuscă makes a fine welcome on fresh bread.

work.summary: Secure and touch up the existing upper shelf. Add the first jars of preserves.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: The pastries keep the lower shelf. The jars go up top, on the left.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Leave the right end free. We will learn what belongs there.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: An empty space on a shelf is an invitation to cook. The cornucopia will fill it with plums.

work.summary: Use one small chalk slate and chalk. Write and draw the first menu by hand.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Bread, mămăligă, cheese, eggs, vegetables, and fruit. From tomorrow, the butcher’s hook gives us pork too.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Draw it, then. Nobody needs glasses to read a picture of soup.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: I will put a copy by the door before the lunch ride.

work.summary: Buy six handmade bowls and six cups with saucers. Wash and arrange them. Keep them for later meals.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: These bowls came from three firings. None is exactly the same blue.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: That is why I like them. Each place will feel considered.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: And each bowl is deep enough for a generous serving.

work.summary: Repair, sand, and refinish the existing long table and two chairs. Keep their sound timber.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: Four people can move this table. Three people can offer advice.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Today all four of us are moving it. Then the old red chairs.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Under that sheet they were painted with birds. A little gold, and they will sing again.

work.summary: Add a notebook and pencils to the existing cabinet. Arrange the recipe corner.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: I brought a notebook for recipes, and my cousin sent legume sacks: beans and lentils for the bean dishes.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Let people add a memory beside a dish, if they want.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: We will leave pencils here. The menu can grow with the neighbourhood.

work.summary: Move the prepared table, chairs, and existing dresser. Clean and set the shared places.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The long table is ready for anyone who wants company.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: I can stop here between deliveries. And I set a fish trap in the stream, so trout goes on the menu.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Your bag may have a chair. Your bicycle must wait outside, and so must the fish.

work.summary: Sweep a small paved courtyard of about 20 square metres. Bag the leaves and clear the path.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: There is a whole courtyard under these leaves. Miez found it before we did.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Our black cat has chosen the sunny wall for a nap.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Let us make the path clear first, then place the tables. Dochia sends lamb down the hill in her shepherd’s bag now.

work.summary: Plant three small herbs in three clay pots with soil and drainage.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: The pots have drainage holes and room for roots.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Lovage and parsley close to the kitchen will be useful.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: And rosemary under the window, where the warmth reaches it.

work.summary: Replace about two square metres of wooden shingles on the sound door hood. Renew fixings and weather seals.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: New shingles, every one. Rain will run off the front, not down the door.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Good. Nobody should have a surprise shower with lunch.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: I will move the pots before we test it with a watering can.

work.summary: Move two existing outdoor tables and chairs. Clean and level them, and keep the path clear.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Keep a wide route from the gate to the door.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Both tables fit along the wall, and the red chairs from the front room came out too.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Now I can carry a tray outside without turning sideways. And the butcher’s block for veal fits by the door.

work.summary: Collect family recipes, copy them onto paper, and pin them above the menu.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Every page describes a different way to finish the same dish.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: We can keep the names of the people who shared them, with their permission.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: And write down what we tried, so the next cook can follow it.

work.summary: Prepare twelve small tasting portions and labels. Use the plates and bowls already bought.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Small plates are ready. There is room for notes beside each one.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: I volunteered to carry them. Tasting was not mentioned, but I remain hopeful.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Finish the delivery, and we will sit down together.

work.summary: Buy the first drinks, fruit, and tea stock and labels. Use the existing niche, pitcher, cups, and glasses.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Socată and fruit tea on one shelf. The traditional spirits on another.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Put clear labels on everything, including the cherry compote.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: Tea for me. There is one more hill on the route home.

work.summary: Print ten sturdy supper menus and add simple stands. Move the existing long table into the courtyard.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: The menu shows a picture of each dish. Anyone can ask what is in it.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The long table is out for the supper. The small ones stay for anyone who wants a quieter seat.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Bring a pencil. A menu always grows by one line after it is printed.

work.summary: Print twenty small invitations. Hang a wreath on the kitchen door. Dress the gate with a lantern and pots of red geraniums, and line the wall with more. Reuse the towels.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: I can deliver the paper invitations along my usual route.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Tell people they can come alone or bring company.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: I will dress the gate so the whole street knows. There is room at the table.

work.summary: Set the existing serving table with a cloth and labels. Prepare the first warm dishes and bread. Reuse the plates.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Plates first, then the warm dishes. Bread belongs at both ends.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: And water where everyone can reach it.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: I have made a little stand for each dish label.

work.summary: Hang one outdoor light string. Arrange gathered wildflowers in existing vases.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Short stems, so nobody has to talk through a bouquet.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: The courtyard lights are on. Two bats are circling above the roof.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: A good evening for them, too. Let us leave their corner of the garden quiet.

work.summary: Top up bread, water, and food for eleven guests. Finish setting places and welcome everyone. Reuse the prepared room and tableware.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The doors are open, the food is ready, and we have a place for everyone.

dialogue.speaker: ilie
dialogue.text: Then it is time to put down the notebook and pick up a plate.

dialogue.speaker: eszter
dialogue.text: Tomorrow we can plan more. Tonight, we share the table.

rooms.label: the unfinished room
rooms.text: The front room at blue hour: the teal tiled stove glows, and the square window looks over the village. Cobwebs hang in the broken window, and a few small spiders keep house on the window web. One small spider lives under the upper wall shelf, by its left bracket.

rooms.label: the mended window
rooms.text: The broken window is fixed: new glass, a cobalt frame and folk-painted shutters. Every web is gone, and the spiders left through the window, all but one.

rooms.label: the welcome board
rooms.text: The welcome board hangs on the wall, mended and painted with folk flowers.

rooms.label: the pastry plate
rooms.text: Round pastries wait on the lower wall shelf.

rooms.label: lamps lit
rooms.text: Both hanging lamps are lit.

rooms.label: polished copper
rooms.text: The worktop is mended, and the copper pans on their pegs are polished bright.

rooms.label: peppers and garlic
rooms.text: Strings of red peppers and garlic from the market hang from the hook beside the herbs.

rooms.label: jars of preserves
rooms.text: Jars of zacuscă and preserves stand on the upper shelf.

rooms.label: the chalk menu
rooms.text: The first menu, drawn in chalk on a small slate, leans on the low cabinet.

rooms.label: blue bowls
rooms.text: Blue bowls from three firings stand beside the jars on the upper shelf.

rooms.label: the painted chairs
rooms.text: The old dust sheet is gone from the corner. Two restored chairs, painted red with gold birds, wait for the long table.

rooms.label: the recipe notebook
rooms.text: A recipe notebook and a cup of pencils sit on the low cabinet.

rooms.label: the painted dresser
rooms.text: The chairs have gone to the shared table, and a small dresser stands in their place.

rooms.label: the swept courtyard
rooms.text: The courtyard behind the kitchen, its cobbled path swept clear of leaves from the gate to the door.

rooms.label: herb pots
rooms.text: Clay pots of rosemary, parsley and lovage stand by the kitchen door.

rooms.label: the new door hood
rooms.text: The wooden hood over the kitchen door has new shingles and sheds the rain clear of the door.

rooms.label: outdoor tables
rooms.text: Two outdoor tables stand along the wall with the red chairs from the front room, leaving a wide path from the gate to the door.

rooms.label: family recipes
rooms.text: Family recipes on loose pages, sketched in coloured pencil, are pinned to the wall above the chalk menu.

rooms.label: tasting plates
rooms.text: Small blue-painted tasting plates wait on the outdoor tables.

rooms.label: the drinks niche
rooms.text: A niche in the thick old wall under the kitchen window holds a blue-painted pitcher, matching cups, glasses and bottles of socată.

rooms.label: the long table
rooms.text: A long shared table now stands in the courtyard for the supper, and a small picture menu, painted with its dishes, stands on every table. The two small tables stay for shyer guests.

rooms.label: the festive gate
rooms.text: A harvest wreath hangs on the kitchen door, embroidered towels drape the gate posts beside a warm lantern, and red geraniums line the wall: there is room at the table.

rooms.label: the serving table
rooms.text: A serving table waits by the kitchen door under a cross-stitch cloth: a stack of folk plates, two lidded earthenware dishes of warm food, and a round and a plaited loaf of bread.

rooms.label: lights and flowers
rooms.text: A string of warm lights runs across the courtyard from the gutter into the walnut tree, and vases of wildflowers stand on every table for the supper.

rooms.label: ready for the supper
rooms.text: The front room is ready for the supper: an embroidered towel hangs across the top of the window, and a jug of wildflowers stands on the dresser. A second black cat sleeps on the counter.

decorations.name: A mărțișor, the red and white string, on the window latch
Willow catkins in a jar on the windowsill
A bowl of red eggs on the windowsill
Green branches tied to the gate

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Your purse looks thin tonight, Mara. Mine too, at the end of the month.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: The night ward needs linden tea, and the herbs cost you nothing. Bring me a cup, and the ward pays for it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: And if the purse is still thin tomorrow?

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Then I come back tomorrow. Patients never run out of nights.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: What if a neighbour walks in and we have nothing to offer? I keep thinking about it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The herbs from the basket cost us nothing. A herb bunch for the water jug, and a linden tea. Cold or warm, ready before they sit down.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Cold and simple. Now, when someone comes in, I will not just stand there and smile.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: You will still smile. But with a glass.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The old woman at the top of the hill says that her dough stopped rising when the frost came.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I promised her two pieces of ours to start from. And a socată for me, because the hill is steep.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Her dough rose before I left. She says that ours woke it up.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Her kitchen clock runs backwards, by the way. She says it always has. I did not ask.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: I have an exam on the nervous system tomorrow, and mine is not cooperating. Shelled corn to crunch while I study, some bread, and a linden tea, please.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: Much better. I can name every bone in the hand now. I counted mine twice to be sure.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: My shift starts at ten tonight. Pogăcele and linden tea will keep me awake until the sun comes up.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: Lovely. If anything knocks on the ward door tonight, it will smell garlic and good bread, and it will go home.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My grandmother cooked on this stove. She said that it sulks if you rush it.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Stoves do not sulk.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then a test bake will prove one of us wrong.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Even heat on both sides. It sulks only at the back now, like a cat.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Fine. It sulks.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I brought my first cups down from the workshop. I threw every one of them on my own wheel.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: One has a crooked handle.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: That one has character. Fill two with water, and we will see who complains.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Not one drop spilled, crooked handle included.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: I am still taking that one home. It looks at me.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: Something in your wall ticks, and it is not one of my clocks. Socată, a langoș, and a whole bread basket, and I will listen to it properly.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: It is a beetle with excellent timing. I have offered it an apprenticeship.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Before we spend a coin, I want to see what the cellar kept for us.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I can hold the lamp. From the top of the stairs.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then we need a snack. Courage is easier with bread.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Two empty barrels, one barrel of Mamaia’s pickles, one good ladder, and a very polite spider.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: It waved. I waved back. It seemed the right thing to do.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: The wind on the hill is still cold, so I am wearing all nine sheepskins. Mămăligă, bread, and a hot linden tea would warm me enough to take one off.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: There. One sheepskin fewer. Eight to go before summer, and the weather is watching me.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In my family, the bread sits where a guest can reach it without asking. Always.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then the new counter is yours. Choose the place.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: I will try each corner with pogăcele. Bread knows where it belongs.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Here, beside the plates. My grandmother kept it on the left too.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Then the left is your corner. Nobody will have to ask twice for bread.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The new window lets the light in. For the first time, I can see my glazes properly.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I made a plate. Put food on it, and tell me honestly if the colour suits it.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Honestly? It suits it.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Good. It looks hungry when it is empty. That is exactly right.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: The snow on the roof is a hand deep. My grandmother said that a roof remembers every winter that nobody cleared.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Everyone on my round admires the snow, and nobody shovels it. It is a commons.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then today we are the commons. Food first, and then the ladder.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The roof is clear. Three neighbours stopped to watch, and all three gave advice.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Advice is free. That is why there is so much of it.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: The university lent me a skeleton to study at home. I set a place for him out of habit. Langoș, mămăligă, and linden tea, please. He will not eat his share.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: He did not eat a bite, so I had both. I think we are becoming friends.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: My mechanical sparrow has learned to steal crumbs. It cannot eat them, but it enjoys the stealing. Some pogăcele and bread, please, and socată for me.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The sparrow took three crumbs and wound itself up with pride. Tick, tick. I will keep the rest.

quests.title: A warm cup at the gate

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: I woke up early. The sun is still up, and I do not trust it. A pogăcea and a hot linden tea, please. The night between the graves is long and cold.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: Thank you. I will tell the graves about you. Do not worry, they never tell anyone else.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: Somebody built a snowman in the churchyard. Each morning, it faces a different grave. A pogăcea, a mămăligă, and a hot linden tea, please. I will watch it tonight.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: At midnight it turned toward the old miller’s grave. I think that they are friends. I gave it my scarf.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: The heating of the night ward broke again. I knit mittens for the patients between rounds. Linden tea and a pogăcea, please, for the knitting hand.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: Eleven pairs of mittens. One patient asked for a third mitten. I did not ask why. I knitted it.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: Monday is Dragobete, when the birds choose their mates. I need a sweet langoș with sugar, cut in two, and a cup of warm milk with two straws. It is for two people. No, I will not say who the second person is.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: The second person was busy at the stove all day, so I ate both halves and used both straws. Please do not tell anyone. Especially the stove.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: We have lamps now. I am afraid that the light makes the plates look tired.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: My plates are never tired.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then let us sit down like guests for once, and find out.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Warm light and a warm plate. I think the room forgives us for the years of dust.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: And the plate looks rested.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Something bit my front tyre on the forest road. Probably a nail.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Probably?

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The tyre has two small holes, side by side. I will think about it while I patch it, and eat while I think.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Patched. I found a nail by the road, and I have decided that it was that nail.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Take the town road tomorrow.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The chimney sweep comes today. In my grandmother’s house, we touched a button of his coat for luck.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I asked him on my round. He keeps a spare button for nervous owners.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: I am not nervous. Bring food for the man on the roof, and something for us.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: He found a burnt page in the flue: half a recipe in Mamaia Paraschiva’s hand, and the words "more pepper than you think".

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: And did you touch his button?

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I only pointed at it. He says that pointing counts for half, so I pointed twice.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: I built a clock that drips the hours from an icicle. Outside, it is very accurate. Near your stove, it runs fast. A langoș, papanași, and a socată, please, while I time it.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: By the stove, it is already Thursday. I will hang it by the door, where time behaves.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: The sheep eat grass all day and never complain. I eat sour cream, and I complain about the grass. Pack me sour cream, pogăcele, and a mămăligă.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: The sheep will smell the sour cream and follow me home. That saves me a walk.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Sunday is the last feast before Lent. At home we had farsang: masks, music, and doughnuts until nobody could stand.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: We have no doughnuts.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Papanași are the doughnuts of the farsang, with better manners. Bring one, and a proper feast around it.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: My mother would approve. She would also ask where the music was.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: I hummed.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: She would not count that.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Two servings of mămăligă with sour cream, please. Ilie says that my new bowls leave no room for a spoon.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: I said my spoon.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: The spoon fits.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: So does a second helping.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: You could have started with that.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: I sold every flower on the cart before noon. Papanași and socată, please, and I can pick more before the bees wake up.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The bees are already waiting by the cart. They like your papanași too.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: An artist has asked me to sit for a portrait. Looking effortless is hungry work. A cheese board, papanași, and a linden tea for me, please, before I return to the chair.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: I sat perfectly still until the tea arrived. The artist says that I am a difficult subject. I prefer interesting.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: I found an old key under the counter, and it hums near the cellar door. Papanași, smoked cheese, and cheese pie, and I will find out what it wants.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: It wanted oil. It stopped humming and started purring. I am keeping it on a ribbon.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Today Lent starts. My grandmother scrubbed every pot on the first Monday, so that nothing of the feast was left in them.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Every pot? We have thirty.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Thirty-one. Fasting food for the scrubber, please: bread, mămăligă, and tea.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Every pot is clean, and so am I, more or less.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Seven weeks of fasting now?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Seven weeks. I will be very polite to the cheese.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Saturday is Women’s Day. In the town, men bring flowers. On my round, the florist has no flowers until spring.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: So you bring sweets.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: To the whole night ward. Ana says that nurses accept sweets on behalf of everyone.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The nurses thank you, Sorin. The doctor tried to accept a papanaș on behalf of the nurses. We stopped him.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Next year I will bring more, and a lock for the box.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: My professor wants proof that I can keep something alive all night. Two eggs and a linden tea should keep me alive, at least.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: It worked. I was alive at sunrise, and the professor is very impressed. He expected a frog.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: My best glaze yet is in the kiln. If I open it early, it cracks.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: So bring me something to eat standing up. My hands need a job.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: It opened, and nothing cracked. Look at that blue.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: She was patient for almost the whole hour. I counted.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: Sunday is the day of the Forty Martyrs. The custom asks for mucenici, and forty small glasses of wine for each man. I tried it once. My pocket clock counted the glasses and stopped at nine. Mucenici and a socată, please.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The mucenici were perfect, and my clock still works. This year, I counted socată.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: On every street of my round, people ask what we will cook here. I keep saying "soon".

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Give me a quick lunch at the counter, and I will have a better answer.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Now I can tell them. Bread that is still warm, potatoes from the new crate, and socată that is cold.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Tell them to come and taste it. That works better than a description.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: The old cathedral on the hill has a staircase behind the altar. It goes down further than the hill is tall.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I pass it on my round. At night, it groans. I always thought that it was the wind.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: There is no wind under a cathedral. We will go down and look, and we need food for several days.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: The pack is full. If we are not back in a week, do not send anyone. Send more pogăcele.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The church clock stopped at half past three. Until I mend it, it is always teatime. Two papanași, please, and a plum for the pendulum. A clock likes things in pairs.

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: The clock runs again. I set it five minutes fast, so nobody is ever late for dessert.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: Spring is close, and I am down to three sheepskins. Bulz, smoked cheese, langoș, and linden tea, and I will give up another without a fight.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: Done. If it snows tomorrow, I am blaming you.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: The first lambs came in the night, two of them in the snow. I will sleep in the fold until the rest arrive. Telemea, bread, and hot tea, please. It is a long watch.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: Seven lambs, all on their feet. The smallest one sleeps inside my coat. That makes ten sheepskins, and the weather is furious.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The long table is ready. What if people sit at the far ends and nobody talks?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then put the food in the middle. People always lean in for food.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: A fruit bowl, then, and a few plates beside it. Something that everyone has to pass.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: They passed it, and they talked. You were right, Ilie.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: My grandmother was right. I only remembered.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: I have three wedding dresses to finish before Thursday. Fruit tea, cherry compote, and whatever the butcher and the market sent, please, before I sew a sleeve shut by mistake.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: All three dresses are done. Joimărița can inspect my house whenever she likes.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: In this village, a candle in the window means that the door is open to anyone.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: On my round, only three houses still do it. The others stopped years ago.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then we will be the fourth. Let us light ours and have supper beside it.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Two neighbours waved, and one of them came in.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: And an owl stared all evening. Nobody invited it. It came anyway.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We are back from the first floors under the cathedral. Dust, bones, and a very large cook with a cleaver.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: He shouted about fresh meat and chased Adrian up two flights of stairs.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: A cook? Did he say where he trained?

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We did not stop to ask. This time, we bring him something better than Adrian.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: We will leave the sausages on the stairs for him. A cook that busy never gets a hot meal.

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: Book my table for eight in the evening. I dine only after sunset, an old family habit. Smoked bacon and two carafes of red wine, if you please. No garlic, naturally.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: Excellent. The wine is exactly the right shade of red. I am very particular about red.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: A table at eight in the evening, please, and not on the same evening as my neighbour. He has moved the fence between our lands again. Roast pork, chicken broth, and red wine. Red helps me read estate papers.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: The papers are in order. My neighbour’s boundary has moved a little toward my land. How odd.

opening.speaker: vlad
opening.text: A guest from abroad comes to my castle soon, on a matter of property. Book my table for eight in the evening, on a night when the countess is not here. I must give him roast pork, tochitură, and plenty of red wine. First impressions matter.

completion.speaker: vlad
completion.text: Splendid. My guest will feel very welcome. Nobody ever wants to leave my castle. Nobody ever does.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Every place at the table has a bowl and a cup. Now the small sweet plate needs its place.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Does it have to be exact?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: It has to look as if it was always there. Bring sweets, and I will move it until it does.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: There. Bowl, cup, plate, and nothing crowds anything.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: You moved it eleven times.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Twelve. The last time was the right one.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I fired a second set of bowls with a green glaze. Ilie says that blue is traditional.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My grandmother had blue bowls.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Your grandmother never saw this green. Fill them, and let the food decide.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: The food likes both. Keep the green bowls with the blue ones.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Tap the bowls on the upper shelf to change them whenever you like.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: My round ends at dawn. Tochitură and roasted vegetables would make a fine breakfast. Or supper. Whichever this is. A second tochitură, please, for the walk home.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: Very good. I will eat it on the way home. My feet know the way.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: The cook ate all the sausages and fell asleep on his cleaver. We walked straight past him.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Deeper under the cathedral, a king of bones sits on a stone throne. He still wears his crown, and he still asks for taxes.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In coins?

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: In bread, it seems. I want to read the marks on his throne, and that is a long reading.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: Sit a while, and listen, I will tell him. Then I will read him his own family history. Nobody stays awake for that.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Everyone in the valley is sending letters this week, and every one of them lives up a hill.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: One letter has no name. Only an address: "the house that is not there".

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Eat first. Then decide what to do with it.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Every letter is delivered. I left the strange one at the crossroads, and by morning it was gone.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Was there a reply?

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: A dry leaf, folded like a letter. I am not delivering that.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: The night patients cannot sleep. A linden tea for them, please, and a proper supper for the porter.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The whole ward is asleep. Even the porter. Especially the porter.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Tuesday is the Annunciation. In Lent it is the first day with fish, and my grandmother never missed it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The fish trap gave us two trout this morning.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then two trout over the coals, and white beans beside them. The cuckoo sings for the first time on this day, too.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The cuckoo sang while I ate. I counted eleven calls.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: What does eleven mean?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: That I ate slowly.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: A gallery is showing my portrait on Friday. I have invited a few friends to admire it. A cheese board, a cozonac, and red wine for the guests, please.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: Everyone admired the portrait. One guest said that its eyes followed her around the room. I hope that she found them attentive.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: We have a courtyard now. My family never ate outside. My grandmother said that the air makes bread stale.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Your grandmother never had a langoș in the sun.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Bring one, then, and a socată. I will find the place where it stays soft.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: By the kitchen door, in the shade. Still warm, and still soft.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I will add a line to her notebook. In small letters.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Before a guest walks the courtyard, I walk it with a full tray. Gate, door, tables.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: And if you trip?

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: Then you will hear it. Put roasted vegetables on the tray, and nettles from the wall. If the route is bad, I want to drop something cheap.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Not one loose stone. The tray reached every chair.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: And then you ate the test.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: A test needs a result.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: The last bus leaves the square at midnight. Nobody gets on after the bridge, but I stop anyway. A langoș and a bulz for the road, please, and a piece of lamb. The lamb is for the horse. Do not ask.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: Thank you. The road through the woods is long, and I like company. Even the quiet kind.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: The bone king fell asleep at chapter two, as Janos promised. Under his throne, the cathedral has catacombs.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: A small goblin lives down there. He begs for mercy whenever he sees us, and he keeps promising us a gift.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: What is the gift?

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: So far, a rock. We will keep watch down there for several nights, so we need proper suppers.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: Most of the bread is for us. One bread basket is for the goblin. Perhaps he will give us a better rock.

opening.speaker: dochia
opening.text: The snow is leaving the high pasture, and the flock wants to climb before I do. Pack enough for the shepherds, the dogs, and me. The ram carries nothing. He says that it is beneath him.

completion.speaker: dochia
completion.text: We reached the high pasture. At the top I took off my last sheepskin, and the wind put it back on me. Next March, then.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: A gentleman from the castle has invited me to a candlelit supper. Cozonac, a cheese board, and red wine, please. His evenings tend to last until dawn.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: A charming evening. My host had no mirrors, so I checked my cravat in a spoon. One must make an effort for good company.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: The new kiln is finished. Potters celebrate by watching it heat up.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: For how long?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Three hours. Bring food for two. You are invited.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: We watched it for three hours.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: And?

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The best party of the year. Do not tell anyone that I said that.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: I finished my thesis at three in the morning, during a thunderstorm. Bring the best of the menu, please. We are celebrating.

completion.speaker: victor
completion.text: My thesis passed. The examiners said it has a life of its own. I am choosing to take that as praise.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: I built new shelves in the cellar, to my grandfather’s plan. Something keeps moving the jars to the left.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Mice?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Mice do not line them up. I will eat a fasting supper down there and watch.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The jars stayed still while I ate. When I went upstairs, they moved again.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: We have agreed to share. My jars on the right, and whoever it is on the left.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: The goblin kept his promise. The rock is a map now. He scratched it himself.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: It shows caves under the cathedral catacombs, and a stream that runs all the way up to your village well.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: So that is why the well water tastes of matches on some mornings.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: We will follow the stream. It is a long path, so we need a large pack.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: Packed. Until we come back, do not drink from the well. Drink cherry compote. It is safer, and it is cherry compote.

opening.speaker: elisabeta
opening.text: I am taking the evening off for a long bath at my manor. Afterwards, a table at eight, please: roast lamb, tochitură, and a carafe of red wine. Do not ask what is in the bath. Rose petals. Only rose petals.

completion.speaker: elisabeta
completion.text: Wonderful. My maids say that I look younger every year. I tell them that it is the tochitură.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My great-aunt’s zacuscă is in the family notebook. She wrote "a good amount of peppers".

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: How many peppers is a good amount?

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Nobody knows. Bring a jar, and lentils beside it, and we will decide for the family.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: This is a good amount. I will write it in numbers, beside her words, for the tasting.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The next cook will not have to guess. She would hate that. She loved a mystery.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Somebody keeps lighting candles in the castle on the hill. It is not my district, but I like to watch with a warm plate. Veal from the new butcher’s block, a bean soup, and a tochitură, please.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: The candles went out at midnight. I stayed awake for all of it. Well, for most of it.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: The painter wants spring light for a new portrait. Tell me honestly, Mara: does my old portrait look tired lately? Cozonac, a cheese board, and red wine, please, while you decide.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: The painter says that I look exactly as I did forty years ago. He meant it kindly, so I paid him twice. The old portrait sighed. I heard it from the stairs.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: On Sunday I sell willow catkins at the church gate. Fish is allowed on Palm Sunday, so I buy it for my sisters. My sisters share very well. Nobody has ever seen them eat.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The catkins are blessed, and the trout are gone. A branch of catkins is for your window. It keeps the storms away, or at least it says so.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I glazed the tasting plates to match the long table. One plum dumpling and a little cozonac will show me if they are large enough.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: And if they are too small?

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: Then the dumpling is too large. My plates are correct.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Room for the dumpling and its label. I was right.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The plates were right. I will clear the test.

quests.title: Holy Week on the night bus

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: In Holy Week, pilgrims fill the night bus. They sing all the way to the monastery, and they ate all my langoș. Two more, please, and a bean soup in a bread bowl.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: The pilgrims blessed the bus, the horse, and my scarf. The scarf did not need it, but thank you.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Your well is clean again. Monica moved a family of very damp lizards out of the stream.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Below the caves, under the cathedral, I found a letter from the archbishop who left this village forty years ago.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: With the money for the church roof. My grandmother never forgave him.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: She was right. In the letter, he writes to someone further down, and he calls them “my lord”.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We will read the rest in the library down there. Its librarian screams when anyone turns a page, but a chimney cake keeps him quiet.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: Thursday is close, and my brother has not touched his spindle. I am taking him zacuscă toast and a langoș, so that he has no excuse.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: He spun all night. Nothing was burned, and nobody had a visitor. A good week.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: I have finished a dancing doll for the village fair. She dances very well, but she stares a little. Cozonac, papanași, and a plum brandy to celebrate?

completion.speaker: costel
completion.text: She danced through the whole fair. Only one child cried, and that was because the cozonac ran out.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: On my day off, I ride through the woods. The horse wants apples. I want zacuscă toast, diced veal, and langoș.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: A fine ride. People ran off the road when they saw us, but I think that was the horse. It is very tall.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: A stranger with a long beard and a book is asking about the weather. I do not like it. Green beans and plum dumplings, so that I can keep watch from the tower.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: He rode off on a very dark cloud. The weather is fine now. Thank you for the plum dumplings.

opening.speaker: dorian
opening.text: It is my birthday. I will not say which one. Cozonac, a cheese board, and a glass of red wine, please, and no candles. There are never enough.

completion.speaker: dorian
completion.text: Thank you. The portrait in my attic sends its regards. It had a much harder day than I did.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tonight the baskets go to the church for the blessing at midnight: pască, red eggs, cozonac, and drob, under an embroidered towel.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: I wove the towels. Sorin carries the candle.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: And I guard the baskets until midnight. I will not taste. Lent is not over.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The priest blessed every basket, and the candle stayed lit the whole way home.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I did not taste. I smelled. Smelling is not in the rules.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Tomorrow, Ilie. Tomorrow you eat first.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: From Holy Thursday until Easter night, the bells rest, and the wooden toaca calls the village. I have nothing to ring, and my hands do not know what to do. Bean dip, green beans, and plum dumplings, please.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I tapped the toaca very politely. Then I sat on my hands until Easter. At midnight I rang so loud that the next valley woke up.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The April rain turned the forest road to mud. It came up to my pedals, and then to my knees.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Take the town road.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The town road has the same mud and more dogs. Something warm, please, before I go back out.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Delivered. The bicycle is still in the forest. It decided to stay.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I will lend you the cart.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: The cart has more sense. It refused.

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: Below the library, the stone under the cathedral turns red and warm. Ilie, you could bake bread on those walls.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Is the heat even?

opening.speaker: adrian
opening.text: Hotter at the back, like your stove. The archbishop is down there. He preaches to an empty hall, and we need one more stay to learn who listens.

completion.speaker: adrian
completion.text: That covers the stay. If you hear a bell ring under the hill, it is only the archbishop. Probably.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Christ is risen, Ilie. The fast is over, and the staff eat together today.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Truly he is risen. Seven weeks of beans, Mara. Last night I dreamed of lamb, and the lamb was very polite about it.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Then lamb, drob, red eggs, and cozonac. You eat first.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: I ate first, and then second. Then I knocked eggs with Sorin and lost every time.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: He holds his egg with the point down. It is a trick.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: It is a sin. A small one. It is Easter.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: I have a bad dream about the supper. The fish reaches the table while the cheese waits.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: In my family, the cheese always went first.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Tonight, both go together. Let us practise one service.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: Together, at last. Now I can watch the guests, not the kitchen door.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: The cheese still went first. By one step.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I know every door on my round. On the supper night, I want to meet each one of them at the gate.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: A meal ready for the first guests who arrive tired from the hill.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: For years, people on my round asked me in for a meal. Tonight, I give each of them one back.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: And then you sit down too.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Then I sit down too.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: On Easter Monday, the young men visit with cologne and sprinkle the girls, so that they do not wilt. Then the girls give them red eggs.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I have a bottle of cologne. A large one.

opening.speaker: eszter
opening.text: A drop is enough, Sorin. One drop.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: I smell like a whole flower market. The cats will not come near me.

completion.speaker: sorin
completion.text: Nobody will wilt this year.

completion.speaker: eszter
completion.text: Nobody in the valley. Here is your egg.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Tuesday is Saint George’s Eve, when the witches and the strigoi walk. It is my turn to hang garlic on every door of the ward. That is a lot of doors. Langoș, pogăcele, and a linden tea, please, before I start.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: Every door has its garlic. The ward smells terrible, and nothing knocked all night. Perfect.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: I am embroidering the towels for the supper gate. Bring stuffed peppers and a fried trout, and I will finish the last corner.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: The towels are done. Each corner has a little red rooster. They keep watch better than Cezar.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: Nobody listens to the archbishop. He preaches to a door, a great red door at the very bottom, sixteen floors under the cathedral.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: Behind it, something snores. The stones shake with each breath.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: So that is the groaning that I hear on my round.

opening.speaker: monica
opening.text: That is the groaning. We go back carefully, and this time we do not knock.

completion.speaker: monica
completion.text: The meatballs are for the archbishop. A man who preaches that long must be hungry, and a full man preaches less.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Last night I woke up in your courtyard with an empty plate. I do not remember eating. Tochitură, mici, and cabbage rolls, please, so that I remember this time.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: I remember every bite. Thank you. If you see me in the courtyard tonight, please wave.

opening.speaker: ileana
opening.text: I embroidered a blue cloth for the serving table. Let us test it with zacuscă and a zacuscă toast. The stains will tell us if it is ready.

completion.speaker: ileana
completion.text: Not a single stain. The blue cloth is yours too. Tap the serving table in the courtyard to change the cloth whenever you like.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: The archbishop ate the meatballs and fell asleep in the middle of a sermon. I borrowed his loose pages.

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: They name what sleeps behind the red door under the cathedral. I will not say that name in a kitchen.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Will it wake up?

opening.speaker: janos
opening.text: Not this year, if nobody knocks. We need a few quiet days to read the rest.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: We will read the last pages down there. When we come back, we will tell you everything over a proper meal.

completion.speaker: janos
completion.text: Until then, if a stranger asks for the way to a red door, send him to the bistro for cozonac.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Today is the Easter of the Blajini. Mamaia Paraschiva always took food to the graves and floated the eggshells down the river.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: Good evening. I opened the churchyard gate early for you. Forgive me, but what is a Blajin?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Gentle little people at the edge of the world. They live so far away that they never hear when Easter comes. The shells tell them.

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: The shells went down the river in a neat line. The graves were very pleased with the colivă.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: You can tell?

completion.speaker: bela
completion.text: After thirty years, you can always tell.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: For the supper, I will ring the bell to call everyone in. That is a lot of rope to pull. Saramură with mămăligă, bean stew, and plum dumplings, please.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: I will ring it loud enough for the whole valley. The next valley too, if they bring a dish.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: Wildflowers are lovely, but lilacs smell like the evening. Bring plum dumplings, roasted vegetables, and fruit tea, and I will bring an armful.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: The lilacs are ready. When the supper starts, tap the jug on the dresser in the front room to change the flowers whenever you like.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Every quest is delivered, and every table is set. Only the supper itself is left to cook: one plate for each guest, to each one’s taste.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: I asked on my round. Vlad and Elisabeta sent their regrets. They do not eat supper, they said. Not this kind.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: Then we are eleven, and the courtyard has ten seats.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: I will stand. A host never sits until the pot is empty. Tonight the bistro cooks, and nobody pays a coin.

opening.speaker: sorin
opening.text: The kitchen is quiet for a moment. Mara says that the staff eat when the kitchen is quiet. Two loaves and two socată, and we sit down for once.

opening.speaker: bela
opening.text: The graves send their regards. Mămăligă and a hot linden tea, please, before the night gets cold.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: My round starts soon. My feet already know the way, but my stomach does not. A bean soup and a loaf, please.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Pickles keep the night nurses awake. Nobody can sleep with a mouth full of pickle. A pogăcea and mixed pickles, please.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: A plain bowl for a fasting man, please: green beans, mămăligă, and a socată. My grandmother would call it a feast.

opening.speaker: victor
opening.text: I read that nettles are good for the nerves. Mine have an exam on Friday. A nettle soup, a loaf, and a linden tea, please.

opening.speaker: costel
opening.text: The church clock wants winding again, and the tower stairs are long. Papanași and two socată, please: one for me and one for the clock. I drink both.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: My sisters are having a picnic in the meadow. Roasted vegetables for two, and plum dumplings for the rest. I will not tell you how many the rest are.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: My sisters thank you, all of them. You may hear singing in the meadow tonight. Please do not go and count us.

opening.speaker: catalina
opening.text: A hail cloud came over the hill this morning. I rang it away, and now my arms are hungry. Zacuscă toast and plum dumplings, please. It is a fasting day.

completion.speaker: catalina
completion.text: Not one hailstone fell on the village. The bell and I can rest until the next cloud.

opening.speaker: ana
opening.text: Tonight is Saint Andrew’s Eve. I will hang the garlic early, and then I want a proper supper: smoked cheese, a langoș, and a linden tea.

completion.speaker: ana
completion.text: The garlic is up and the plates are clean. Let anything knock tonight. We are fed, and we smell of garlic.

opening.speaker: sanziana
opening.text: It is almost Midsummer Eve. We dance until dawn, so we need plum dumplings and zacuscă. Dancing is hungry work.

completion.speaker: sanziana
completion.text: We danced until sunrise and wove a crown for you. It hangs on the gate. Do not wear it after dark.

opening.speaker: bran
opening.text: The town has a pumpkin fair this weekend. Last year I carved the best pumpkin head. People said that I understand heads very well. A langoș, minced veal, and cabbage rolls, please.

completion.speaker: bran
completion.text: The langoș is for the bus. The rest is for me. The pumpkin head is for anyone who needs one.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: My grandmother pickled everything that stood still long enough. I want to fill the cellar jars her way.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: Her way takes all afternoon.

opening.speaker: ilie
opening.text: That is why I need a proper lunch first.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: Full and labelled, in her order. Cabbage, then peppers, then plums.

completion.speaker: ilie
completion.text: One label says "Do not open before winter". I did not write that one.

opening.speaker: cezar
opening.text: Tonight is the longest night of the year, and I walk all of it. Tochitură, bean soup, and a sharing board, please. One bite for every hour.

completion.speaker: cezar
completion.text: The sun came up at last. I counted fourteen hours, two owls, and one shadow that walked home with me. It was polite.

opening.speaker: ionatan
opening.text: I have come from abroad to close a real-estate deal with a local noble at the nearby castle. Before I continue, I would like a proper dinner.

completion.speaker: ionatan
completion.text: An excellent dinner. Here is the payment, with my thanks. My papers are in order, and I must leave for the castle now. My journey takes me on from there, so I will not return. Farewell.

opening.speaker: mina
opening.text: Ionatan is my fiancé. He came from Britain to sign a property contract at the castle, but he has not written back. Have you seen him?

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: He had dinner here and left for the castle. He has not returned to the bistro.

opening.speaker: avram
opening.text: Then Mina and I will follow that road together. Before we leave, could you prepare a meal for two?

opening.speaker: mina
opening.text: No meat or fish, please. Eggs and dairy are fine.

completion.speaker: mina
completion.text: Thank you for the meal and for telling us which road he took. We must find out why his letters stopped.

completion.speaker: avram
completion.text: We shall leave for the castle together now. I have my medical bag, should he need help.

completion.speaker: mara
completion.text: I hope you find him safe. Take care on the road.

dialogue.speaker: sorin
dialogue.text: There is news going round the village. Mina and Doctor Avram found Ionatan gravely ill. All three have left for Britain. They did not stop at our bistro on the way back.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: Then he is no longer alone. I hope he recovers at home. Thank you for bringing the news, Sorin.

events.title: The funeral meal
events.line: Cook the funeral meal (pomană) for Mamaia Paraschiva, in the village. It is a fasting day.

scene.text: The village churchyard in snow. Mourners with candles stand before the church, among them Mara, Ilie, Eszter, and Sorin, beside a table with colivă and colaci.

opening.speaker: mama
opening.text: The colivă and the colaci are ready. Put them on the tray for the priest. He blesses them before anyone eats.

opening.speaker: mara
opening.text: The mourners come in from the cold churchyard. A bean dip for the fasting table, with plenty of garlic. Mamaia said that garlic keeps out the cold, and other things too.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: The telephone rang on Friday, on Saint Ignatius. Mamaia Paraschiva died in her sleep, in the village, in the house above her old bistro.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: She was ninety-one, and she still made her own colivă. She said that a colivă from a shop has no memory.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: The funeral is on Monday. We cook here in the city and drive it to the village. Colivă and colaci for the table of the dead, and beans, because it is a fasting day.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: I have not been to the village since I was twelve.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Then the village has not seen you since you were twelve. Wash your hands.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: After the meal, I walked down to the bistro. The shutters are closed, and the sign has lost two letters.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: A black cat sat on the steps, as if he waited for the door to open.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: That is Miez. He was your grandmother’s. Nobody knows how old he is. She did not know either.

dialogue.speaker: mara
dialogue.text: When we packed the car, he was in my bag. He did not ask.

dialogue.speaker: mama
dialogue.text: Then he comes with us. A cat that chooses a bag has chosen a family.

events.title: Christmas Eve
